Ana: Heads up — the reservation queue for west-eu GPU pool just jumped again. We're at 42 pending. Most are short-term experiments. Can we consider soft-reserve -> burst conversions to reduce lead time and invoice churn? :eyes:
Tariq: 42 matches what I see. There are 28 <24h hold requests, 8 for a week, 6 long-term. Lead time on new reserved commits is 3–4 weeks for node fulfillment.
Ana: Ugh. Any quick wins?
Tariq: We can do two things: 1) auto-convert small requests (<24h expected runtime) to burst slots if pool has slack, 2) prioritize resume for any request with SLA tag = production. Need sign-off on policy.
infra-bot: Queue snapshot: pool=west-eu g5x16, pending=42, available=6, avg_wait=2.9d. Actionable: 14 requests eligible for burst.
Danya: If we move non-prod to east-us2 burst we save ~25% on burst pricing and free west-eu for prod. But some teams need low latency.
Zack: Reminder — some experiments pin to west-eu datasets. Latency/regional affinity matters. We should avoid blind relocation.
cost-ops: Quick cost delta I ran: reserved (monthly amortized) ~ $3.8k/GPU-month, burst (on-demand pool) ~ $0.95/hr. For bursts used <72h it is cheaper than converting to a short monthly reserved commit. Example: 48h of burst ~ $45 vs prorated reserved ~ $250. So bursts win for ephemeral loads.
cost-ops: math: 48h * $0.95 = $45.6 vs (30d * 24h * $3.8k/720h) ~ $250.
Ana: That helps. Proposal: auto-approve burst for requests flagged "experiment" and age <24h, notify requester with opt-out window 30m. Convert only if pool availability >2 nodes.
Tariq: Sounds good. Need a safe guard: don't convert if requester has "region_lock" tag. Also ensure KV cache warming disabled for bursts (we lose KV if preempted).
Danya: I'll draft the conversion flow and a short notice template.
Katie: Can we also add a billing hook so cost-ops sees spikes from burst conversion in real-time? Last month's invoice had a weird +12% variance and we want to correlate. @cost-ops
cost-ops: Yep — I'll open a billing investigation ticket and hook the burst-policy logs into the cost dashboard. Ticket: BILL-4872.
Ana: Operational checklist: (1) policy + opt-out msg (Danya), (2) implement region_lock check (Tariq), (3) billing hook (cost-ops), (4) dry-run for 24h to observe churn (Katie). Who owns rollout?
Tariq: I'll own the code change and dry-run. ETA 48h to PR.
Danya: I'll post the opt-out copy in #eng-infra and #devex.
cost-ops: I'll correlate last invoice and watch for anomalies during dry-run.
Katie: Let's convert top 2 short requests for the dry-run in 1h and notify owners. If anything breaks we revert. :thumbsup:
Ana: Agreed. Please log actions in the ticket and ping me if any production-affecting evictions occur.
infra-bot: Action executed: converted 2 eligible requests -> burst pool. Owners notified.
Zack: Watching perf. No immediate complaints.
Ana: OK closing this thread for now, monitoring window 24h. Thanks all.
